neighbours.label: ' high' or ' higher' opening a compound modifier before a noun in technical writing ('used for high-temperature', 'covers higher-order'), not 'high' as a plain predicate
fire: This alloy is used for high-temperature turbine blades.
The lab specializes in high-resolution imaging of cells.
Students in the seminar learn about higher-dimensional spaces and their geometry.
The paper describes a method for high-throughput gene screening.
We built an engine from high-strength steel plates.
The course treats higher-order logic and proof systems.
The team works on high-voltage power lines in rural areas.
A theory of higher-category structures appears in chapter nine.
quiet: This alloy is used for low-temperature turbine blades.
The lab specializes in low-cost imaging of cells.
Students in the seminar learn about curved spaces and their geometry.
The paper describes a method for rapid gene screening.
We built an engine from thick steel plates, and its price is high.
The course treats basic logic and proof systems.
The team works on rural power lines where the cost is high.
The fees described in chapter nine are higher.

notes: Probes: attributive ' high'/' higher' 0.17-0.43, predicative 'are high' 0.07, ' low' near zero. The token cannot see the hyphen that follows it, so what it reads is the attributive slot.
